name: bonk-sir-a3-rising-cut
notes: Sir Bonk air.3 (anim.bonk.a3, the player's aerial 2), 2026-11-01: the aerial partner of the ground Rising Cut (tools/genra/briefs/bonk-sir-g3-rising-cut.json), replacing Air Sunrise, whose plank never went below his feet and rose behind his head from the game camera. Authored at twice the game length (80 ticks for a 40-tick move: hit 12-19, late auto-cancel from 28, free 40). v2 pack bonk-unity-sirv2rise. Owner approved keys run 20261101-181151 on 2026-11-01 ("looks better go for it").
character: Sir Bonk v2 (a Humanoid body with Mixamo names, index-finger chains only besides the thumbs; a 3x4 cape chain Cape_L/C/R1..4 under Spine2 that a spring drives in the game, so leave it at rest; a 1.42 m plank greatsword fixed to the right hand as joint Weapon0, with bladeHilt at the crossguard and bladeEnd at the tip; a pot-lid pauldron fixed to the left upper arm as joint Weapon1). The right pauldron, a big round pot lid, is part of the body mesh and sits out over the right shoulder joint: keep the right forearm and hand out of it.
description:
Sir Bonk's aerial 2, the Air Rising Cut: in the air, one fast one-handed cut that rises from below his boots on his left, across the front of him, to high over his right shoulder. It is the aerial partner of his ground Rising Cut and the mirror of his Air Squire's Cut, which cuts down across the front. It catches people under and in front of him on the way down and people above him.

Why. His old aerial 2 never brought the plank below his feet (its tip stayed 0.38 m above his boots) and its hit rose behind his head from the game camera. This one must start low, below his boots, and sweep up across the front where the camera behind him sees it (image 3 shows the ground version's path from that camera).

Who he is. Sir Bonk is a goofy, good-hearted wannabe knight (image 1). Normals stay clean: no gags; the energy comes from his body.

His fall pose, where this move starts and ends (reference 'fall', tick 0; character frame from his hips): the plank rests back over his right shoulder, the right hand in front of the right chest (0.30 m right, 0.29 ahead, 0.45 up), the tip 0.96 m to his right, 0.42 m behind and 1.98 m above the hips. The right knee is lifted (right foot about 0.54 m below the hips), the left leg hangs (left toes about 1.06 m below the hips), the left arm out for balance. The game moves the fighter through the air: no root motion, lift, hover or forced dive; local hip shifts and counterbalancing legs are fine. The feet never plant on an imaginary floor.

How the game plays it. Authored at twice the game's length: 80 ticks here play in the game's 40. The plank itself is the hitbox from tick 24 to tick 38 here (game 12-19): the cut must be crossing in front of him for all of those ticks, with its fast part inside them; the cocked pose is held at ticks 20-22 and the cut starts moving at 22-24. From tick 56 (game 28) a landing cancels the move cleanly, so ticks 56-80 are the fall pose exactly (`b.exit_pose`).

The path, seen from behind him (the `gameplay` view): one sweep across the screen from low left to high right. Nothing goes behind him and nothing swings toward or away from the camera. The draw is short and low: it does not swing over his head.

The beats:
- Ticks 0-20, the draw: the plank leaves his shoulder by tipping forward and down in front of his right side (the tip stays right of his centre line and drops away from the camera), then the right hand carries it low across his belly to his left hip. At tick 20 it is cocked low on his left: the blade points down and forward to his left, the tip below his boots (at least 0.9 m below the hips), ahead of or beside his left foot, never behind him. His chest turns about 35-45 degrees to his left, he tucks a little (both knees up, compact), the left arm swings back. Hold briefly at 20-22.
- Ticks 22-32, the cut: fast. The hips whip right first, the chest follows, the legs swing the other way to counterbalance, and the right arm drives the plank up across his front. At tick 28 it crosses straight in front of him, pointing forward at chest height. By tick 32 it is high on his right.
- Ticks 32-38, the finish: the arm extends up and out to his right, the blade 60-75 degrees above level over his right shoulder, the tip above his helmet and not behind him. The body opens out with the reach.
- Ticks 38-56, home: the plank tips back onto his right shoulder into the fall pose, the legs return to the fall pose. A normal's recovery is plain: the shortest calm path, no flourish. Ticks 56-80 are the fall pose exactly.

The plank stays clear of his bucket, crest, pauldrons, cape and legs. Fast motion belongs to the cut (ticks 20-40). Use the toolkit's flow functions for follow-through. Do not animate the cape joints. Keep each hand in line with its forearm (wrists under 45 degrees).

The draw (ticks 0-20) rolls the right hand and upper arm a long way (plank from resting on the shoulder to tip-down at his left hip). The ground take of this move failed once on a twist flip there: spread that roll over the whole draw with breakdown keys (for example ticks 5, 10, 15) solved from the neighbouring key (solve(..., seed=previous_key)) with the plank carried between them (solve.carry), so no limb bone rolls more than about 30 degrees in a tick. No swing over his head in the draw.
